summary.text: Michael Howe is North Dakota's Republican Secretary of State and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.

A former state legislator first elected in 2022, he said in a July 2026 interview that North Dakota's elections are secure, pointing to proof-of-citizenship checks at ID issuance, paper ballots and encrypted result reporting.

paragraphs.text: Howe is a fifth-generation farmer who helps run his family's seed farm near Casselton, and he graduated from North Dakota State University in 2010.
He worked in Washington, D.C., as agriculture policy director for Rep. Rick Berg.
Howe later served as a state representative for District 22.
He has been North Dakota's secretary of state since January 1, 2023, and was the Republican candidate in the November 3, 2026 general election.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election for Secretary of State of North Dakota with 62.1% of the vote to Ryan Braunberger's 37.9%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
